translations.text: [?] they dispute in doubt [?] the Son of God. Thus indeed said the prophet: "[?] to his [?] whom you seek, whom you desire."
that he is born of the Father, is named the Son of God, [?] is read [?] to be announced beforehand, [?] the same Father foretold [?], saying:
and [?] you to the place that I have prepared.
[?] you sin against him [?]
Who then is this angel who held power with the Lord God among all the sons of God? That same one is certainly the Son,

who, ever sent from the Father, later showed himself to the sight of men. From this same sending he is called an angel. Isaiah also, more openly, confirmed this same Son born of the Father, when he said:
"The voice of the Lord repaying recompense to his enemies," signifying those same Jewish people who do not believe. Thus also said the prophet:
"Before" [?]
[?] gave birth, and before it came upon her she bore a male child."
Thus the same prophet said openly: Before the virgin bore Christ in the flesh,

the Father begot the Son in his divinity; and before the virgin's time came to give birth, the Father begot him without any beginning of time. About this the prophet said afterward: "Who has ever heard, or who has ever seen anything like this, anything at all among men that is in any way like it?"
And afterward he said: "Shall I, who make others give birth, not give birth myself? said the Lord.
"And shall I, who give others to bear, be barren?" With all this testimony it is [?]
[for him] who does not believe, that he choose one of two things: either to believe Christ the Son of God, or [to hold] false the prophets who foretold this.
OF THIS IT SPEAKS HERE: HOW CHRIST WAS BORN INEFFABLY OF THE FATHER BEFORE CREATION.
Many are seeking at what time the Son of God was born, yet he is eternally existing, just as is written about him: "His going forth" [?]

"nor the circuit of the earth of the world. When he made ready the array of the heavens, I was there; when with a sure law he encircled the waters of the abyss, when he weighed the foundations of the earth," [?]
I was with him then, making all this."

With testimonies of such great majesty it is now so openly made clear that Christ, the Son of God, was born of the Father before all ages. It is then now made known that through him, from the almighty Father, everything that is created came to be. Yet they now seek this anew:

how this same one was born, since in his holy birth the mystery of the Father is so hidden. No apostle tells this, nor did a prophet discover it, nor did an angel of God know it, nor did any creature perceive it.
Isaiah confirmed this where he said: "Who shall declare Christ's birth?"
Therefore now, if the prophet of God could not declare Christ's birth, who will presume to understand how the Son could be born of the Father?
About this same thing it is also said in the books of Job: "Where do you find the wisdom of the divine Father? It is hidden from the eyes of men, and it is concealed from all that fly in heaven."
It is indeed unknown even to the angels themselves.

As is also written there: "To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed?" That root is indeed the origin of God's Son. Since this is truly beyond the understanding and knowledge of the exalted angels, what man could then explain it?
It is certainly for us to know now that to the Father alone it is fully known how he begot the Son,

and to the Son, how he was born of the Father. In the same way they also now seek an account of this begotten Son, because there is no son unless he is born of two. And the perishing creation of mortals has the beginning of birth in this same manner.
But Christ came from the Father truly in this way, just as brightness from the sun, as a word from the mouth,
as wisdom from the heart.
HERE IT SPEAKS OF HOW CHRIST IS GOD AND LORD.
Now that the almighty mystery of God, the divine birth of Christ, has been proclaimed, we will immediately go on to make it known to you with clear examples from holy scripture
that Christ himself is indeed God and Lord.

But if Christ were not God, to whom was it said in the Psalms: "Your throne, O God, is from eternity to eternity; the rod of righteousness is the rod of your kingdom. You loved right and hated wrong; therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions"?
Who, then, is this God anointed by God?

Let the unbelievers answer us now. See, here it says that God was anointed by God, and Christ is indeed meant by that same anointing where it says that God was anointed. When you hear of the anointed God, understand truly
that Christ is meant there, just as Christ is indeed named from the anointing with chrism.
About this same Christ the almighty Father proclaimed through Isaiah,
though he spoke in the name of Cyrus, that he is God and Lord:

"Thus said the Lord to my Christ Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, that I may bow nations before his face to him, and I will turn the backs of kings to him, and I will open doors before him, and the gates will not be shut. I will go before you and subdue for you the glorious ones of the earth. I will shatter gates of bronze, break iron bars, and give you the hidden treasure, and I desire that you understand the holy mystery. For I am the Lord, who names you, the God of Israel."

In the name of Cyrus, Christ is certainly foretold, before whom nations and kingdoms are bowed down into the faith. In no other way was anyone ever named Cyrus in the kingdom of Israel. If then anyone believes

that this was foretold of Cyrus, king of the Persians, let him recognize that it is repugnant and heathen for anyone to believe that this lawless man and worshipper of the heathens' idols should be named Christ, God and Lord. Moreover, concerning this it is not so written in the translations of the Seventy:
"To my Christ Cyrus"; rather, they write:
"This the Lord said to my Christ the Lord." And it is now beyond doubt and plain to understand that this is said in the name of our Lord.
If Christ is not God, let the unbelievers now tell us to whom God was speaking in Genesis, where he said: "Let us make man in our image and in our likeness."

As is also said there afterwards: "And God created man; in the image and likeness of God he made him." Let them now ask again which God created him, or in whose divinity he made in his image the man whom he created.
If they answer and say "in that of the angels":
But surely an angel is not equal to God?

There is so very great a difference between the likeness of the creature and that of the one who created everything. Or could an angel make man just as God did? Believing that would be great madness. So to whom is this said, or in whose likeness was man created, if not in the likeness of the one
who is equal to God and bears the same name as God?
And again, if Christ is not Lord, which Lord rained fire on Sodom from the Lord?
As it is certainly written in Genesis: "And the Lord rained brimstone and fire from the Lord upon Sodom and Gomorrah."

In this saying let no one doubt that this is certainly the second person of God, the Lord Christ himself. And who then is that Lord, if not truly the Son from the Father? He was always sent from the Father and used to come down from heaven and go back up.
This testimony shows in clearer light both the one divinity and the distinction between the two persons, Father and Son.
Now if Christ is not Lord, concerning whom did David say in the Psalms:
"The Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right side"?
Although Christ, in the body of the flesh, is David's son, yet in the Holy Spirit he is certainly God and Lord.
If Christ were not Lord, about whom did David say in the Books of Kings:
"Thus said the man to whom it was granted, the noble psalmist of Israel, concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob: The Spirit of the Lord speaks through me, and his word through my tongue"?
If, then, Christ is not Lord,
who is the Lord of hosts who was sent by the Lord of hosts?
As he himself said through Zechariah: "Thus said the Lord God of hosts: He sent me after glory to the nations that plundered you.

Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye. See, therefore I lift my hand over them, and they will become plunder for those who once served them, and you will know that the Lord of hosts sent me."

Well now, whose voice can this be, if not that of the saving Lord? He, the almighty God, declared himself to have been sent by the almighty Father. He was certainly sent to the nations in this way according to the glory of his Godhead, which he held together with the Father. When he emptied himself and took on the form of a servant, he became obedient unto death. The same one also, following on here, said: "Praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion, because behold, I come and will dwell in your midst, says the Lord. And on that day many nations will be gathered to the Lord and will become my people, and I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you."

Which, then, is this Lord sent by the Lord of hosts, if not again that same Lord, the Savior Christ? Moreover, also earlier here, concerning the Holy Spirit, concerning his Godhead and that he is the Spirit of God, Job spoke thus:
"The Spirit of the Lord made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.

See, God made me just as he made you." Concerning that same Spirit he had certainly said before: "The Spirit of the Lord made me." He then joined that to God when he said afterwards: "See, God made me just as he made you."
By this he made known that this same Spirit is God.
HERE IT SPEAKS OF THE INDICATION OF THE THREE PERSONS OF GOD

It is shown in the books of the old law that the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are God. But the Jewish people do not believe that the Son and the Holy Spirit are God, because they heard God's voice loudly on Mount Sinai, saying:
"Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one God."
They do not understand how in the Trinity there is one God, Father and Son and Holy Spirit. They are not three gods at all; rather, in these three persons there is one name of the undivided power.
Let us now seek this same Trinity again in the old Holy Scripture. In the first part of the books of Kings it is certainly written thus: "David the son of Jesse said, the man said,

to whom it was commanded concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob, the excellent psalmist of Israel: The Spirit of God is speaking through me, and his word goes through my tongue." And immediately after that he openly showed who the Spirit is, when he said:
"The God of Israel spoke to me, the righteous ruler of men, the strong one of Israel."

Where he said "the Christ of the God of Jacob," he certainly meant the Son and the Father. And where he said "The Spirit of God speaks through me," he meant there, clearly recognizable, the Holy Spirit.
Again, David also spoke of this same thing in the Psalms: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the spirit of his mouth all their power stands."
In the name of the Lord we certainly recognize the Father; in the Word we believe in the Son. In the spirit of his mouth we certainly understand the Holy Spirit.
In this testimony the number of the Trinity and the communion of their single work are truly shown.
As the same prophet said hereafter:

"He sends his word and melts them; his spirit breathes, and the waters flow." See, here he now means three: the Father is the one who sent, and the Word is what was sent, and his Spirit is the one who breathes.
And also in Genesis it says: "In the beginning God made heaven and earth, and the Spirit of God hovered over the waters."
There, too, the Father is to be understood in the name of God; in "the beginning" the Son is to be recognized, because he himself said:

"At the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do your will." God is the one who spoke, and God is the one who acted. And moreover, in that he hovered over the waters, he signified the Holy Spirit there.

Indeed, so also, certainly, where God said, "Let us make man in our image and like us": through the plurality of the persons the sign of the Trinity is revealed there. And yet nevertheless, to show the unity of God, he said here right afterward: "God made man in his image."
And also when God afterward said, "Behold, Adam has become like one of us": that same plurality of naming shows the mighty mystery of the Trinity.
The prophet Haggai showed the holy mystery of this same Trinity in this way, speaking in the Lord's name: "My Spirit shall be in the midst among you."
Behold, God spoke there; behold, his Spirit is also meant immediately after that. Concerning the third person, who is from the Son, the same prophet spoke thus:
"For behold, I shake heaven and earth, and the desired one will come to all nations."

In the same way, the separate distinction of each of the persons is also shown in the books of Isaiah, when the Son of God himself says: "I am the first and I am the last. My hands also made the earth, and my right hand measured the heavens. And from the beginning I was speaking in secret, from that time, and before any time came to be, I was there." Immediately after that he also said:
"And now the Lord God and his Spirit have sent me." Behold, here two of the persons,
God and his Spirit, who did the sending; and the third person is that of the Lord Christ himself, the one who was sent.
So also in another place, through the same holy prophet, the sign of the Trinity was shown in this way: "God said: See my servant, I receive him; my beloved, my soul is well pleased in him.
I have given my Spirit upon him." There the Father meant his Son when he named the beloved servant upon whom he gave his Spirit.
Concerning this Spirit, the Lord Christ the Savior testified with his own voice when he said: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me."
And in another place Isaiah himself also took in the whole Trinity by a counting of fingers, when he preached and said:
"Who measured the water in a single handful? And who weighed the heavens with his palm? Who weighed the whole globe of the earth with three fingers?"
Indeed, in three fingers the holy prophet weighed the threefold coequality of the almighty Godhead, with the balance of a certain mystery.
And also, by the power of equal might, he made known in three fingers the shared work and the unity of the almighty efficacy, which is one and the same in the Trinity.

In another place the same prophet also made known that he recognized the mystery of the Trinity, when he said this: "I saw the Lord sitting on a very high throne, and the seraphim, the angels, stood above him.

"Each had six wings, one six and the other six. With two they covered his face, with two they covered his feet, and with two they flew." The prophet also showed that the same Lord is threefold in his persons and made known that he is one in his Godhead, for after this he said of the angels:
"And they cried out to one another, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts. The whole earth is full of your glory."

See here now: the heavenly host praises the threefold holiness in a single confession. Yet with the threefold saying the seraphim meant the one glory of the Trinity. For what else is meant where the three "Sanctus" are spoken, if not that the glory of that same almighty Trinity is shown? And yet, although the sign points to three persons of God, we must not believe that there are three gods, as there are three persons;
rather, in the three persons we must truly proclaim one Godhead, according to the words of Moses, where he said:
"Hear, Israel: the Lord your God is one God." And again it is also written:
"I am the only God, and besides me there is no other."
HERE IT TELLS HOW GOD BECAME MAN: CHRIST, THE SON OF GOD
Up to this point we have shown the spiritual mystery of the heavenly birth in Christ and the meaning of the divine Trinity.

From here on, let us make known with the authority of holy scripture that the Son of God himself was born in a body. First of all, let us show how the Son of God himself became man in the likeness of flesh for our salvation.
As Isaiah said, preaching about him:
"A child will be born to us, a son will be given to us, and his lordship will be upon his shoulders, and his name will be called Wonderful, Counsellor, mighty God, Father of the world to come,
Prince of peace. His rule will be multiplied, and of his peace there will be no end."
The prophet certainly meant this of Christ's lowliness, because he was born for us and not for himself. For certainly, his becoming man helps us, and so he was born for us.
Again, a son was given to us. Whose son, if not God's? His dominion is upon his shoulders,
both because he carried his cross on his own shoulders and because Pilate wrote the title of his kingship above his shoulders and his head.

But now let the impious be ashamed, and let them acknowledge and name Christ the Son of God, and believe him begotten, and become little through the taking on of the body. David said about him: "You made him a little less than God." For while he was in the form of God, he did not then judge it any fall [?] that he was equal to God.
but he emptied himself when he took on the likeness of a servant."
To him the Father then said in the Psalms, concerning his eternal birth: "From the womb, before Lucifer, I begot you."
Then immediately afterward he showed his future birth in the flesh, when he said: "And just as from the bearing womb, so springs forth the dew of your youth."
This incarnation of the Son of God the Holy Spirit also in the Psalms
Thus he made known, where he said: "To Zion one said, and a man will be born in her, and he himself made her, he the Most High."

See, he who was born in Zion, and who in that same city became the humblest of all, that same one is the Most High, who made her. And also how this same one is the Lord: it is written afterward there: "The Lord told the record of the peoples: this one was born there."

Who then is this man who was to be born there? Certainly it is the Most High and the Lord. Man, because God became man. Most High, because the heavens and the angels receive him as above themselves. He is also Lord, because all the creatures of heaven and earth serve him.
It is true that as often as the enemies of Christ hear these holy prophecies about Christ's birth, they are always so trapped that they have nothing at all to set against them.
Unless they then argue that Christ has not yet come, of whom the ancients sang all this long beforehand through the mouths of the prophets.
So let us now look for the time of Christ's birth, whether he has already come or whether we must still wait for him to come.

In the scripture of holy Daniel the coming of Christ is shown precisely and the years are counted out, and his signs are openly proclaimed beforehand, and there it is also said most openly how the destruction of the Jews was to come after Christ's birth and after his passion. There it is certainly shown so precisely,

As the angel of God said to the holy prophet: "Daniel, take heed of this word and understand this vision. Seventy weeks are shortened upon your people and upon your holy city, so that the perverse transgression may be ended,

and that there may be an end of sins, and iniquity may be destroyed, and eternal righteousness may come, and vision and the message of the prophets may be fulfilled, and the Holy of Holies may be anointed." Certainly now, if those seventy weeks are counted from the time of Daniel, without any doubt it is then recognized,
that the Holy of Holies of all the holy, the Lord, Christ the Saviour, has already come long ago.
But in the holy sayings a week fulfils seven years. As the Lord himself said to Moses: "Count for yourself seven weeks of years."

That means seven times seven, in which are counted together one less than fifty years." But from the time of Daniel the prophet up to the time of Christ's coming itself, more than a hundred and forty weeks are counted,
and therefore Christ, whom the prophet's word proclaimed beforehand, has certainly already come.
After the seventieth week, it is openly shown here that Christ had truly already been born and martyred, and that the city of Jerusalem was laid waste, and sacrifices and anointing ceased.

As the same prophet indeed says after this: "And Christ will be slain, and the people with the leader who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. And its end will be desolation. And after the end of the war, desolation [literally "emptinesses"] will be set there." All this truly came to pass,

when Titus came after Christ's passion, won victory over the Jewish people and destroyed the city and God's temple. And then the offerings of their sacrifices ceased, which they could never again hold there in their congregation. So it was fulfilled as it had been foretold earlier through the prophet.
But because they slew Christ out of the hardness of the Jewish mind, they do not want to believe that he has even come yet.

We have now certainly shown here that our Lord, the Saviour Christ, was already born according to his bodily birth. But the unbeliever still asks and says: Why was Christ born in a body? Now hear the reason why. When God first created man, blessed with the highest blessings and honoured with the beauty of the divine likeness,
he then set him in his paradise, so that he would be obedient to God and be above God's other creatures.

But he then became disobedient, and in contempt of God he defiled the commandment that had forbidden him. God did not slay him when he was cast out of there for his arrogance, but made him an exile from the bliss of paradise. The Almighty still waited then, so that through repentance he might again make himself ready for salvation.
And when he again did not turn back to the way of his former virtue, God then gave Moses the law, so that by it he might yet turn back to the love of God and to works of righteousness.
But when he then, arrogant and unbelieving, did not even keep that same law:

then at last the Son of God came for this reason and took on a human body, so that when they saw him in person they might at least believe in this way, and so that the world might abandon the devil's deceptions and be moved back to the grace of its Creator.
This is the reason for the birth of Christ,
whom the Jewish people, though they believe him to have been born, nevertheless revile as having been nailed to the cross and put to death.

They do not understand that just as he, the Christ, was said to be born for the redemption of the world, so likewise it was also said that he was to be martyred for the salvation of the earth. His martyrdom and death we find with the testimonies of holy scripture,

when in other passages we go through what is to be said here before that. Now, however, let us follow the discourse we have begun. And of this same Christ, the birth of whose humanity following upon his godhead we have already gloriously made known, let us now also make known his descent and lineage.
LET US ALSO FIRST BEGIN TO SPEAK ABOUT HIS NAME
First, the name of Jesus was found, signified beforehand in prefigurations of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For that reason indeed Hoshea the son of Nun was named by Moses with the name Jesus.
This same man received the lordship of the people of Israel when he became its leader after the death of Moses and divided among them the lands of the inheritance promised to them.
What did the change of name signify? Only that, after Moses was dead and the law had passed away and the old commandments of God had ceased, our Lord Jesus Christ was to become our leader,

who, having sanctified us through the stream of the Jordan, that is, through the gift of holy baptism, with all kinds of sins driven out and all the hosts of evil angels put to flight, leads us through into the promised land,
where honey and milk flow, that is, into the riches of eternal life, for nothing is sweeter than that.
Therefore indeed the son of Nun received the likeness of the holy mystery, in that he was named Jesus as a prefiguration of the true Jesus. Concerning him it is written in the Psalms:
"Come and let us praise the Lord; let us sing with shouting to God our Jesus."
Here it is shown that Jesus is the Lord, concerning whom it also says in another place, in a psalm: "The Lord takes pleasure in his people, and he exalts the meek in Jesus."
This is certainly said in this way in the Hebrew scripture.
HOW OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST ALSO CAME FROM THE SEED OF ABRAHAM.
Genesis tells what Abraham's command to his servant was:
"Put your hand under my thigh and swear by the God of heaven." In these words he proclaimed beforehand concerning Christ, the heavenly Lord, that he was to come in the flesh of his lineage.

By the thigh is indeed to be understood offspring. It thus signified that the heavenly God was to come in the flesh from the seed of Abraham. In his seed it was promised to him by the Lord, through Isaiah, saying:
"In your seed all nations shall be blessed," that is, in Christ.
Of him the psalmist said: "And in him all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed; all nations shall praise him."
And concerning that seed the voice of the Lord said through the same Isaiah: "I will bring forth from the seed of Jacob, and from Judah, him who shall possess my mountains."
Concerning this also, in another place, the same prophet said: "Unless the Lord had left us seed."
AND WHY CHRIST WAS AWAITED IN THE FLESH OF THE TRIBE OF JUDAH.
Jacob the patriarch said prophetically:
"A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs,
until he comes who is to be sent, and he himself is the expectation of the nations." It is indeed true that, until the coming of Christ's birth,

the Jewish people did not remain without rulers from the tribe of Judah, nor without a leader from his thighs, until Herod, the foreign king. He, in desire for the kingdom, through the seizure [?] of power [?].

As soon as that was done, the leadership from the seed of Judah ceased, and he came who was to be sent, for whom nations and peoples were waiting. But the Jews, in their fierceness and with shameless malice, say lyingly that the time is not yet fulfilled, though I know of no king from the lineage of Judah, nor any ruler in the outermost ends of the eastern realm.
Blind in mind, they take no notice that their false lies have been exposed. For just as no temple remains to them anymore, nor any altar, nor any sacrificial offering,
so likewise no king and no priest remains to them, the Jewish people.

Nor can the prophet Hosea be lying in any way, who said through the Holy Spirit: "The sons of Israel shall sit without king, without lord, without sacrificial offering, without altar, without priesthood, without revelations."
Who is there who does not see all this now fulfilled in them?
HERE IT TELLS HOW CHRIST WAS BORN OF DAVID'S DESCENT
Behold, let us now learn from what lineage Christ was to be born,
to come from the descent of David according to the measure of the flesh, through the Holy Spirit,
as was foretold of him in the psalms:
"The Lord swore to David in truth and did not deceive him: The fruit of your womb I will set upon my throne."
"Once I swore by my holiness:
I will not lie to David; his seed shall dwell forever. And his throne is like the sun before my face, and forever like the full-grown moon,
and he is the faithful witness in heaven."
So also in another place it is written in Paralipomenon:
"And the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying: Go and say to my servant David:
Thus said the Lord:
I tell you that the Lord will build you a house. When you have fulfilled your days, so that you go to your forefathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from your sons,

and I will establish his kingdom for him. He himself will build me a house, and I will make his throne firm forever. I shall be to him in the place of a father and he shall be to me in the place of a son,
and I will not take my mercy from him,
as I took it from that one,
who was before you.
And I will establish him in my house and in my kingdom unto everlasting eternity. And his throne shall be most firm forever."
Whoever supposes that all such things were fulfilled in Solomon understands very wrongly.
For how is it to be understood of Solomon that it was said thus:
"After you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you,
who shall be from your sons,
and I will establish his kingdom for him"? It is by no means to be believed that this was foretold of that Solomon, who certainly began to reign while his father was living.
But here it says:

"For when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed." From this it is to be understood that another was promised there, because he was not foretold to be raised up before David's death, but only after his death.
Concerning him the Lord himself said through Jeremiah:
"Behold, days are coming, said the Lord, and I [?]

I will raise up for David a righteous offspring, and he, a king, shall then reign and will be wise and will carry out judgment and justice on earth. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel too shall dwell confidently.
And this is his name, as they shall call him:
this is our Lord, the Righteous One."
He who was promised through Nathan from the seed of David, that same one was also foretold through Isaiah the prophet:
he said:
"A rod shall grow up from the roots of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root."
He said this because he was indeed from the land of Bethlehem, of the kin of David.
This rod from the root of Jesse is the undefiled virgin Mary, come forth from the root of David, who bore the flower.
the saving Lord.
Concerning the same one it also follows afterwards:
"And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him,
the spirit of wisdom and of understanding mind, the spirit of counsel and of might, the spirit of knowledge and of mercy."
and the spirit of the fear of God shall fill him."
So many gifts of the Spirit are foretold concerning him because the Holy Spirit does not dwell in him by measure, as it does in us.
Rather, in him is all the fullness of the gifts of God and of the Spirit.

This is he who "does not judge according to the sight of the eyes and the hearing of the ears, but righteousness is the girding of his loins and faithfulness is the belt of his reins." In his kingdom "the wolf dwells with the lamb," and also he who was accustomed to drag plunder away from the kingdom.
once he has been converted, makes his dwelling with the innocent.
In his law "the leopard lies down with the kid": this signifies the malicious mingled with the sinful.
There also "the calf," from the Jewish law,
"the lion," from worldly power, and "the sheep," from the rank of humble people, "dwell together" with the stronger in the church of Christ, because there, in the true faith, all share a common life.
"A little child shall drive all of them again":

That is indeed he who humbled himself for our sake, just as a child. "The ox also and the lion shall eat chaff there together," because the highest, together with the lowlier people, have common teachings there.
"The child was longing, from its mother's breasts, over the hole of the asp."
This signifies

that the peoples who were once accustomed to preach poison, these, turned again to the gentleness of children, took delight in hearing the faith of Christendom. "The hole of the adder" indeed signified the minds and wills of the unbelievers,
in which the crooked serpent rested,
which [?] of the word of God,
Christ, having seized it, dragged out from there, away into exile,
so that it "on Christ's mountain,"
that is, the kingdom of Christendom,
"shall not harm."
Here too the same prophet Isaiah speaks further about Christ, how he was born of David's seed according to the measure of the flesh,
as he says hereafter:
"On that day the root of Jesse shall stand as a sign to the peoples; the nations shall pray to him, and his grave shall be glorious."
The root of Jesse stands as a sign to the peoples when Christ presses the sign of the cross onto their foreheads.
The nations pray to him, which you now see fulfilled before you.
His grave, moreover, is so very venerable
that we,

Whom Christ fetched, for that redemption in return for his death we rightly and honorably bear honor to the place. And that same place also shows by wondrous signs the matter of his venerable power, and draws all the world to him.
This place is also meant in the Hebrew scripture: "And his resting place shall be honorable." So it certainly is that, when he died, his flesh saw no corruption.
As it is said according to the saying of the Psalmist:
"You will not allow your holy one to see corruption."
